THE FINDING -- THE CAPACITY GATE WAS THE ONE ENTRY CONSTRAINT THAT LEFT NO RECORD, AND MEASURING IT CLOSES A QUESTION RATHER THAN OPENING ONE. live.py guarded the whole S2 block with "if s2_at_risk < strategy2.MAX_TRADES:" and NO else. When the book was full the block was skipped entirely -- including the "scanned N coins -- no mean-reversion setup" heartbeat two levels down, which exists precisely so a quiet scanner is distinguishable from a dead one. So the log was byte-identical for "we looked and found nothing" and "we never looked", and only the second costs a trade. Every other gate (RSI, ADX, stretch) leaves a record; this one left none. MEASURED by joining position intervals from state.json against the scan stream -- possible only because a SEPARATE loop prints RSI/ADX per coin every hour regardless. Over 918 scan-hours: 0 positions open 558h (60.8%), 1 open 327h (35.6%), 2 open 33h (3.6%). Inside those 33 blocked hours the gate-qualifying rate was 2.02% (8 of 396) against 0.47% (55 of 11686) when the book had room -- 4.3x baseline, Poisson p~0.002 against the pooled rate. THE CONFOUND IS THE FINDING: the book is full BECAUSE setups just fired, so "book full" and "another setup qualifying" share a cause (market-wide dislocation). This is the 2026-08-19 cluster (three shorts in three hours into one pump, two concurrent, both losers) seen from the other side. Capacity binds exactly when opportunity clusters, and what clusters is CORRELATED -- so it is an argument about correlation, not a case for raising MAX_TRADES. SIZED HONESTLY: RSI+ADX is an upper bound on qualifying (the scan line carries no stretch term), so the report deflates by the MEASURED conversion -- 21 trades opened per 55 reachable qualifying obs = 0.38 trades/obs. MAX_TRADES=2 therefore cost ~3.1 trades over six weeks, ~+0.52R at meanR +0.171. VERDICT: THE CAP IS NOT THE FREQUENCY BOTTLENECK.
